articles.title: From Canvas to Code: Building a Multidisciplinary Art & Tech Brand as a Solo Creator
articles.excerpt: Body As a visual artist and founder behind Iceberg Art Nation, my day-to-day work spans two worlds that are often treated as completely separate: traditional physical fine art and modern digital archi…
articles.body: Body As a visual artist and founder behind Iceberg Art Nation , my day-to-day work spans two worlds that are often treated as completely separate: traditional physical fine art and modern digital architecture. On one hand, I spend hours mixing acrylics on canvas and working with physical pencils. On the other, I manage e-commerce storefronts, design digital character concepts, deploy smart contract assets across decentralized networks like Base, and experiment with model context protocols (MCP) to manage digital collections. I'm sharing this breakdown to explore how independent creators can leverage developer tools, Web3 provenance, and smart infrastructure to turn traditional craftsmanship into a scalable, tech-enabled brand. 1.

articles.body: Varsovie en voxels : la 3D interactive qui cartonne sur Hacker News — et ce qu'elle révèle sur votre vision La « Show HN: Warsaw in voxels » grimpe à la 18e place avec 263 points. Une carte 3D interactive du centre-ville, rendue en voxels, explorable dans le navigateur. C'est fluide, impressionnant, open-source. Le rendering GPU utilise une structure octree pour le culling spatial, streaming progressif des chunks, shaders optimisés pour le voxel traversal. Beau travail d'ingénierie. Mais il y a un angle qu'on oublie : pour en percevoir la vraie profondeur, il faut deux yeux qui savent fusionner leurs images. Environ 3 % des adultes vivent avec une amblyopie (œil paresseux) — souvent non diagnostiquée à l'âge adulte. Le cerveau a appris à ignorer l'œil le plus faible.

articles.title: All 25 of our tables have row level security on and not one policy, and that is the finished design
articles.excerpt: A Supabase project gives you two ways into the same Postgres: a connection Nakodo only uses the first one. This $ grep -c "enableRLS" src/db/schema.ts 25 $ grep -ric "create policy" drizzle/ 0 $ grep…
articles.body: A Supabase project gives you two ways into the same Postgres: a connection string, and a public REST API that anyone holding the project's public key can call from a browser. Nakodo only uses the first one. This is the census of what that means in the schema, and the part that surprised me when I checked it. The census $ grep -c "enableRLS" src/db/schema.ts 25 $ grep -ric "create policy" drizzle/ 0 $ grep -ri "pgPolicy" src/db/schema.ts | wc -l 0 25 tables, 25 calls, no policies anywhere in the schema or in any of the 32 migrations. In the generated SQL the calls show up as one statement per table: ALTER TABLE "campaigns" ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY ; --> statement-breakpoint There are 28 of those statements, spread over 9 of the 32 migration files.

October 2026 brought us PHP2Shell, Node2Shell, and a poisoned LiteLLM release. Well, also a GitLab CVE, and an NGINX CVE, and an OpenCode CVE—you get the picture. Actually, we had more high and critical CVEs in October 2026 than we had in the whole of 2021 . Welcome to Docker Security Dispatch 8, reviewing October 2026. This month: two shells, a compromised release pipeline, the growing gap between exploitation and patching, and some Docker commands to help us survive the next security apocalypse. Plus, some discount codes for books, a meetup in the Black Forest, my adventures at BaselOne, and a trip to J-Fall!

articles.body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority When we first went hands-on with Qualcomm’s new Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 processor back in September, its headline features had me excited. With CPU clock speeds reaching 5GHz, a massive 16MB Oryon Flex Cache, and Qualcomm’s next-generation Adreno GPU, the chip promised a major leap in performance for demanding workloads such as emulation and gaming. articles.body: TL;DR Google is working on a new “RAW images” section in Google Photos’ Collections tab. This section will display all the RAW images backed up in Google Photos. The feature isn’t live right now, but we managed to surface it with some tinkering. Most Android phones these days can shoot RAW photos right out of the box. articles.body: As the time-afflicted Link comes to learn in the seminal Nintendo 64 classic, a lot can change in seven years. Shifting political struggles leave a neighborhood in total disrepair. That one local eccentric he came to love is nowhere to be seen. There’s a Starbucks — or an archery range, I mean — in town now. Seriously? articles.title: The Taurid meteor shower peaks tonight — and fireballs could steal the show
articles.excerpt: The Taurid meteor shower could spawn dazzling fireballs in the coming weeks! Here's when and where to look.
articles.body: Heads up stargazers! The Taurid meteor shower is upon us, bringing multiple peaks of activity that could see spectacular shooting stars and fireballs brighten November's sky. Here's where and when to look. What is the Taurid meteor shower(s)? Every autumn, Earth plows through streams of debris left behind by Comet Encke, a 3-mile-wide (4.8-kilometer) ice body that orbits the sun once every 3.3 years. These debris streams produce two branches of the Taurid meteor shower : The Southern Taurids, active from Sept. 20 to Nov. 20 and the Northern Taurids, active from Oct. 20 to Dec. 10. As Earth plows through the debris streams, tiny particles slam into our atmosphere at 65,000 miles per hour (104,607 kilometers per hour), producing dazzling streaks of light across the night sky.

articles.title: NASA asks industry for ideas about saving Hubble Space Telescope
articles.excerpt: The Hubble Space Telescope is healthy but is being pulled down toward Earth by atmospheric drag. NASA is considering options to extend the iconic telescope's work.
articles.body: NASA is reviving discussions to rescue the Hubble Space Telescope, which is operating well but is on track to reenter Earth's atmosphere about six years from now. The agency issued a request for information (RFI) on Oct. 29 for "in-space servicing" capabilities, which could include boosting Hubble's orbit (which is naturally degrading due to atmospheric drag), or even a mission to "enhance its capabilities" in some way. Hubble, which launched in April 1990 in partnership with the European Space Agency , was serviced five times by astronauts on space shuttle missions, the most recent being in 2009.

articles.title: Ancient star collisions could explain mysterious Little Red Dots and 'impossible' black holes
articles.excerpt: Collisions between stars in the early universe were common, and this could explain the growth of supermassive black holes and the existence of strange Little Red Dots seen by the James Webb Space Tele…
articles.body: New research suggests that collisions between stars in the early universe were common, which could help explain the rapid growth of supermassive black holes and the existence of strange Little Red Dots seen by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). The team behind this research performed simulations of the early universe and found stellar systems were densely packed, leading to stars frequently slamming into each other. While rapid collisions would have destroyed the stars involved, slower collisions would have led to repeated mergers, creating single over-massive stars, which could collapse and form larger-than-usual black holes at the end of their lives. These could be the seeds of the first supermassive black holes.
